pr_title: jobs: enable marking jobs as idle for metrics
pr_body:
In order to allow long-running / indefinite jobs to not continually
block a tenant from being treated as inactive in a serverless
environment, this change adds a MarkIdle API to the jobs registry which
increases / decreases a counter of currently idle jobs. An idle job
should be able to be shut down at any moment.  Through the CurrentlyIdle
and CurrentlyRunning jobs numbers serverless can determine if all jobs
are idle and the tenant can be safely shut down.  For now this is only
saved in-memory in the registry object, however we may transition to
saving in persisted job state as well in
the future.

Fixes #74747

Release note: None
pr_comments: This change is [](https://reviewable.io/reviews/cockroachdb/cockroach/75897)

issue_context.title: jobs: Add MarkIdle API
issue_context.body:
A running job may want to mark itself Idle.  And idle job may be shutdown.
MarkIdle should increment a counter keeping track of the number of idle jobs.

Initial Design for the purposes of allowing CDC to function on Serverless:
- A `jobs_[type]_currently_idle` metric will track the number of idle jobs of that type.  Using metrics allows for serverless to not rely on the jobs table
- For now, idleness state will only be stored in the Registry rather than worrying about persisted state yet.
- Idleness should not be updated more often than twice a minute (so jobs should wait at least 1 minute since becoming active before marking themselves idle again).  This allows changes to idleness state to be logged.

This doesn't allow for observability into individual jobs, but this can easily be added as followup.

Epic CRDB-8671
comments:
Can we stipulate how quickly / often we expect jobs update their idle change state? Is this like progress updates, where a job is expected to keep its own local state and then update after say 15s or 1m in which it did no work, or is it expected to e.g. be able to update in every iteration of a select loop?

What about non-changefeed jobs? Any reason we're making a `jobs_changefeeds_currently_idle` metric vs just a `jobs.currently_idle` metric?

> Can we stipulate how quickly / often we expect jobs update their idle change state? Is this like progress updates, where a job is expected to keep its own local state and then update after say 15s or 1m in which it did no work, or is it expected to e.g. be able to update in every iteration of a select loop?

For Changefeeds I currently have a `changefeed.idle_timeout` cluster setting that defaults to **10 minutes**, where if the frontier hasn't been notified that any aggregators have emitted any kvs since more than 10 minutes ago, it'll mark the job as Idle.  As soon as the frontier is informed that a kv was emitted, it'll set the idleness to false.  Aggregators inform the frontier of how many kvs were emitted at the same time they send resolved spans. 

I don't imagine jobs would realistically changing their idleness state quickly? since the purpose of this "idleness" is "Its been long enough that its unlikely any work will happen in the near future".  I suppose it depends on the cost of tearing down a node/tenant and bringing it back up, which I don't have a good understanding of.

> What about non-changefeed jobs? Any reason we're making a jobs_changefeeds_currently_idle metric vs just a jobs.currently_idle metric?

Ah sorry, edited it now to say `jobs_[type]_currently_idle`, its only that way because all I did was add a `CurrentlyIdle` Gauge to `pkg/jobs/metrics.go`, which is already split by job type.

If the expected usage in changefeeds is that they won't be setting idleness until 10min, then I'd go ahead and add something to this API contract now that a single job should not switch its idleness more than, say, twice per minute -- that still leaves room for immediately becoming active after setting idle, as long as one waits >1min to set idle. Having that property codified now leaves more room for updating persisted progress later with idle state and makes it reasonable to log a message when idleness changes, which seems like a good idea so we can correlate if  things start happening right after a job became active, just like we can if a standard job starts executing for the first time and logs it "entering state running" message.
Makes sense 👍 , by "add something to this API contract" would a code comment suffice or do you mean enforcing it at runtime?
Just a comment seems fine to me, ala `A single job should not call this method more than twice per-minute as it logs and may write to persisted job state in the future`
Posting here to follow along; going to cargo-cult whatever we do for the AUTO SPAN CONFIG RECONCILIATION job: https://github.com/cockroachdb/cockroach/issues/70538.

I would probably doe if log.V(1) -- this just seems to be too verbose. We don't seem to log normal job behaviors, transitions in states, etc.  This seems to be normal.

So I think I argued for logging these state transitions in the issue. We log, today, when a job starts running ("stepping though state running..."). This is useful since you can now look at a log and go "aha, the job started running at 123, and as 124 we see these things explode". If a job is moving from idle/parked into active work, that is potentially equally notable to when it initially started running, if idleness is defined on a long enough time-scale; in conjunction with the contract above that says you can only change state twice a minute, I think you can argue this logline isn't too spammy.

This seems wrong to me: you probably should not increment multiple times even if MarkIdle(true) called multiple times.  And decremented below 0 would also panic.  I suggest we add a test for exactly this type of behavior.
This should already function that way since it'll only inc/dec if `aj.isIdle != isIdle`, so multiple `MarkIdle(true)` fail that.  I'll add the below-0 error and a test around this :+1:
